question: From a point P on a level ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 30°. If the tower is 50 m high, the distance of point P from the foot of the tower is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°−60°−90°** triangle, the ratio of sides opposite to these angles is **1 : √3 : 2**.

The side opposite to 30° (height) is **1 unit = 50 m**.

The side opposite to 60° (distance from foot) is **√3 units**.

Distance = 50 × √3 = 50√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 50√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/089eb26a165d0879463bd54aeddb0c3edaf7cb4cfa76250a55b3712380c1e68e.png] 

**Given:**

Height of the tower (QR) = 50 m

Angle of elevation at point P (θ) = 30°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

**Calculations:**

⇒ tan 30° = QR / PQ

⇒ 1 / √3 = 50 / PQ

⇒ PQ = 50 × √3

⇒ PQ = 50√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 50√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Common values: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

Angle of Elevation vs Depression

The **angle of elevation** from an observer to an object is equal to the **angle of depression** from the object to the observer due to alternate interior angles.

Standard Triangle Ratios

For a 45°−45°−90° triangle, the side ratio is 1 : 1 : √2. For a 30°−60°−90° triangle, it is 1 : √3 : 2.</p
